1.deliverable: A one-to-two page application brief (brief.md) that someone else could build from without guessing.
setup: Install Git, then clone Taskboard to compare your work with a finished brief.
Create a brief.md file for your own idea (or follow along with Taskboard's).

code.title: Get the example
code.body:
git clone https://github.com/solomonpromise/taskboard.git
cd taskboard
cat docs/brief.md

code.title: Ask AI to review, not build
code.body:
Here is my application brief. Do not write any code.
List every question a developer would need answered
before starting, and point out contradictions or
vague requirements. Number your findings.

2.deliverable: A diagram of your application's parts plus a written trace of one user action from click to database and back.
setup: Clone Taskboard and run it locally (commands below).
Open http://localhost:5173, create an account and add a task.

code.title: Run Taskboard locally
code.body:
git clone https://github.com/solomonpromise/taskboard.git && cd taskboard
make install   # packages + backend/.env
make migrate   # local SQLite database
make dev       # backend :8000, frontend http://localhost:5173

code.title: Watch one request
code.body:
1. Open Developer Tools → Network.
2. Create a task in Taskboard.
3. Click the request to /api/tasks and note: method,
   status code, request body and response body.
4. Compare with docs/api.md.

3.deliverable: A running copy of the project, a short map of its folders, and one small change committed on its own branch.
setup: Create a free GitHub account and fork Taskboard so you can open pull requests.
Clone your fork into a brand-new folder and follow only the README.

code.title: Fresh setup from the README
code.body:
git clone https://github.com/<you>/taskboard.git taskboard-fresh
cd taskboard-fresh
make install
make migrate
make test
make dev

code.title: A deliberate change
code.body:
git switch -c tweak-empty-state
# edit frontend/src/pages/TasksPage.tsx
git diff
git commit -am "Clarify empty task list message"
git push -u origin tweak-empty-state
# open a pull request on GitHub

4.deliverable: A compact design pack: system diagram, technology choices with reasons, data model, integrations and quality trade-offs.
setup: Have Taskboard's brief, architecture and decision records open for reference.
Create a docs/ folder in your own project for your design pack.

code.title: Decision record (docs/decisions/00X-name.md)
code.body:
# Decision: <what was chosen>
Context: what forced a choice
Options considered: A, B, C
Choice: B
Why: 
Trade-offs accepted: 
Revisit when:

code.title: Ask AI to challenge the design
code.body:
Here is my design pack. Act as a sceptical reviewer.
Find contradictions, unsupported requirements, risks and
unnecessary complexity. Cite the section for each.

5.deliverable: A working first version built in small, reviewed steps, with tests passing and a log of what AI produced and what you checked.
setup: Pick an AI coding tool and point it at AGENTS.md and docs/design.md first.
Work on a branch; make sure make test passes before every merge.

code.title: Task prompt (format from docs/templates.md)
code.body:
Read AGENTS.md and docs/design.md first.
Goal: let a signed-in user mark a task as done.
Scope: routes/tasks.py, services/tasks.py, TaskRow.tsx.
Do not: change auth, add packages, touch other pages.
Done when: the change persists after reload and a test
proves another account gets 404 for my task.

code.title: Check every increment
code.body:
make test
git diff main
git commit -am "Toggle task done"
git push   # then open a focused pull request

6.deliverable: A live deployment plus a maintenance guide covering monitoring, backups, recovery and how to make future changes safely.
setup: Make sure make test passes and the app runs with make start.
Optional: install Docker to run the production-style setup with PostgreSQL.

code.title: Rehearse a release locally
code.body:
make test
make start                       # production-style on :8000
make smoke URL=http://localhost:8000
make backup                      # writes to backups/
